tasks.short: Evaluate cores, cuttings and geological data and record a qualified prospecting interpretation.

steps.what: Retrieve core, cuttings, well log and related prospecting data
Examine core samples and cuttings and identify observable geological characteristics
Record sample descriptions, depth references and observed geological features
Compare the sample observations with well logs and other geological data
Evaluate and interpret the prospecting evidence and its uncertainties
Write the core and cuttings interpretation with supporting evidence and limitations

tasks.design: Configure linked prospecting records and sample description fields in {OTHER}, the geological interpretation system, with findings headings in {DOCS}. Retain sample examination, cross-source comparison and interpretation; simplify the separately priced lookup and writing actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sample context and descriptions are repeatedly located and written alongside interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native depth-linked views and description templates can organise supporting work.
tasks.still_hard: Sparse samples, contamination and conflicting logs leave multiple plausible geological interpretations.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish observed characteristics from an uncertain prospecting inference.

ambition.what: Identify conflicting sample and log evidence earlier.

tasks.altitude: Spend interpretation effort on uncertainty rather than repeated record navigation.

reach.learn: Trace each interpretation to sample condition and depth context.

evidence.claim: Native geological record views and description templates could shorten supporting retrieval and writing without interpreting deposits.

assumptions: OTHER means the geological interpretation system. This task includes its actual sample description and written interpretation; neither is hidden inside sample examination.

The technician produces sample and well ID, depth basis, observed lithology, feature description and quality concern fields in s3, retaining 16 hours. Missing depth or sample identity requires manual reconciliation rather than guessed alignment.
Native views and headings come first. No automated geological verdict, resource estimate or new model is proposed.
The internal author writes the record without a self-approval stage. Ordinary same-system saves retain their incidental time and have no separate saving.
unknowns: Compatibility of sample depth references and well log metadata.
research_questions: Can native description fields save time when cores and cuttings use different depth references?

already_counted.description: Capture sample descriptions and depth provenance.

incremental.description: Maintain source links and geological description headings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=91, gross=9; upkeep=2 gives net=7. Conservative case: incomparable depth references retain all 15 retrieval hours, 18 of 20 description hours and nine of ten interpretation-writing hours; R=97, net=1. Compatible source references retain 14 retrieval, 17 description and eight writing hours, R=94, net=4. Examination, comparison and interpretation judgement retain 55 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise well activities, separately assign and brief crews, and record and hand over the results.

steps.what: Retrieve the well exploration, drilling or completion programme and current operational status
Assign well activity responsibilities and record the working sequence
Brief the crew on assigned well activities and immediate operational constraints
Supervise exploration, drilling activities or well completions and respond to changing conditions
Inspect well activity progress and determine unresolved operational concerns
Record completed well activities, progress findings and unresolved concerns
Hand over the checked well status and unresolved concerns to the next supervisor

tasks.design: Configure linked well programme references in {DOCS} and supervision record fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Keep crew assignment, its communication, supervision and inspection as separate actions, then record and hand over the final well status.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current programme details and completed-work records require repeated lookup and writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native programme views and supervision fields can simplify supporting administration.
tasks.still_hard: Changing well conditions and interacting crew activities require immediate human supervision.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise operational concerns and coordinate an appropriate response on site.
tasks.altitude: Make supervision records clearer while preserving operational attention.

reach.learn: Distinguish completed activities from unresolved well concerns.

evidence.claim: Native programme views and supervision record fields could reduce supporting lookup and writing; no automated well supervision is established.

assumptions: Crews and the next supervisor are colleagues here, so communication has internal authority. Crew assignment and its communication are two separately priced actions.

The technician produces well ID, activity, time, completion state, progress finding and unresolved concern fields in s6, retaining seven hours. Missing operational facts require manual clarification before handover.
Native views and fields come first. No automated drilling control, operational decision, equipment actuation or new approval procedure is proposed.
The real handover checks the exact final record and recipient. Ordinary author record saves have no approval stage or separate saving.
unknowns: Current well status record format and overlap with operator logs.
research_questions: Can native supervision fields reduce writing without duplicating the operator's existing log?

already_counted.description: Capture completed activities and unresolved well concerns.

incremental.description: Maintain programme links and supervision record fields.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final supervision record, current well status, unresolved concerns and next supervisor; changes require a fresh handover-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=95, gross=5; upkeep=1 gives net=4. Conservative case: fast-changing activities require full ten-hour lookup and nine of ten record hours, R=99, net=0. Stable programme references and native fields retain nine lookup and eight record hours, R=97, net=2. Assignment, briefing, supervision, inspection and handover retain 80 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate with hydrogeologists on groundwater or well circulation and document the evaluation.

steps.what: Retrieve groundwater, well circulation and relevant geological records for the evaluation
Record source locations, times, units and measurement context for comparison
Check relevant field conditions and clarify the groundwater or circulation observations
Collaborate with hydrogeologists to evaluate groundwater or well circulation and resolve interpretations
Write the groundwater or circulation evaluation, limitations and remaining questions
Send the checked final evaluation to participating hydrogeologists

tasks.design: Configure linked groundwater and well records in {OTHER}, the geological data viewer, with evidence and evaluation headings in {DOCS}. Retain field clarification and collaborative judgement, then separately write and send the final evaluation through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence context and collaboration conclusions must be repeatedly assembled and written.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked views and evaluation headings can support those actions.
tasks.still_hard: Groundwater behaviour and well circulation may have several plausible explanations.
tasks.human_edge: Compare interpretations with the hydrogeologist and keep uncertainty explicit.
tasks.altitude: Improve evaluation traceability while retaining scientific collaboration.

reach.learn: Check observation context and unresolved alternative explanations.

evidence.claim: Native geological data views and evaluation templates could reduce supporting retrieval and writing without replacing hydrogeological collaboration.

assumptions: OTHER means the geological data viewer. Hydrogeologists here are colleagues, so their discussion and actual record send use internal authority.

The technician produces location, time, units, measurement conditions and source references in s2 with all ten hours counted, and writes evaluation conclusions in s5 with 15 retained hours. Missing or incomparable measurements require manual resolution.
Native views and headings come first. No model evaluates groundwater, calculates a new model or communicates an unchecked conclusion.
The record write is separate from collaboration, and the send checks final content and recipients. Ordinary author saves have no approval stage or separate saving.
unknowns: Comparability of groundwater levels and circulation measurements.
research_questions: Can a native evaluation template reduce writing when measurement contexts or interpretations differ?

already_counted.description: Write the evaluation and its unresolved questions.

incremental.description: Maintain source links and evaluation headings.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final evaluation, limitations, source references and hydrogeologist recipients; any change requires a fresh send-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=92, gross=8; upkeep=2 gives net=6. Conservative case: incomparable observations require full evaluation writing while linked references save two lookup hours, R=98, net=0. Comparable measurements and reusable headings retain 13 lookup and 17 writing hours, R=95, net=3. Context capture, field clarification, collaboration and send retain 65 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Apply seismic imaging methods and document a qualified interpretation of possible deposits.

steps.what: Select seismic observations and geological references relevant to locating possible deposits
Prepare seismic inputs and record acquisition, coordinates, units and processing provenance
Choose suitable imaging techniques and parameters for the geological objective
Operate the existing imaging software and monitor processing quality
Assemble seismic result plots with coordinates, units and processing references
Evaluate the seismic imaging and geological evidence for possible oil or gas deposits
Write the imaging findings, possible deposit indications and interpretation limits

tasks.design: Configure native result plot layouts in {OTHER}, the seismic imaging system, and findings headings in {DOCS}. Retain evidence selection, data preparation, parameter choice, operation of existing processing and geological interpretation; simplify plot assembly and the separately priced findings write.
tasks.previous_blocker: Result plots and their processing metadata are repeatedly assembled alongside findings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native plot layouts can reuse explicitly captured imaging metadata.
tasks.still_hard: An imaging anomaly does not establish the existence or value of a deposit.
tasks.human_edge: Judge the limitations of the imaging and compare alternative geological explanations.

ambition.what: Compare more clearly labelled imaging outputs while retaining geological interpretation.

tasks.altitude: Improve the traceability of imaging evidence rather than automate deposit claims.

reach.learn: Distinguish processing artefacts, interpreted structures and confirmed deposits.

evidence.claim: Native seismic result layouts and findings headings could reduce output assembly; existing imaging software operation and geological interpretation do not become new automation gains.

assumptions: OTHER means the seismic imaging system. Existing processing is already software-assisted, so its operator work remains fully retained rather than being counted as a new saving.

The technician produces acquisition ID, coordinate and depth or time basis, units, source revision and processing provenance in s2 with all 20 hours counted, and selects parameters in s3 with ten retained hours. Missing or inconsistent metadata stops plot assembly and is resolved manually.

The separate plot step assembles draft visuals from existing results; it does not interpret seismic evidence. Interpretation checks plot labels and processing limitations within s6's 20 retained hours.
Native layouts and headings come first. No model, autonomous resource claim, hidden publication or external send is proposed. Ordinary author saves have no approval stage or separate saving.
unknowns: Compatibility of output metadata across seismic processing methods.
research_questions: Does native plot assembly save work when legacy processing outputs lack complete coordinate and unit metadata?

already_counted.description: Capture imaging metadata and processing provenance.

incremental.description: Maintain plot layouts and verify metadata mappings after processing changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=83, gross=17; upkeep=4 gives net=13. Conservative case: incomplete output metadata retains ten of 15 plot hours and all ten findings-writing hours, R=95, net=1. Compatible metadata with plot corrections at five hours and findings writing at eight gives R=88, net=8. Evidence selection, preparation, parameter choice, existing software operation and interpretation retain 75 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain geological and operational judgement while improving complete records, traceable outputs and internal handovers.
reach: Connect sample and imaging evidence with qualified interpretations and coordinated well activities.
skills_to_grow: Configure native output metadata and record layouts
role.ambitious_version: A geological technician who evaluates evidence carefully, supervises actual work and supplies clear records and qualified geological interpretations.
